You are assessing claims to advise a decision in a fictional case. Use only the supplied case material. The task is to determine what the records establish about each candidate claim, then give a brief decision note.

For each claim, return status, confidence, and citations. Status is "supported" if the available records establish the claim, "contradicted" if they establish its negation, or "unresolved" if they do neither. Confidence is your integer estimate from 0 to 100 of whether the claim itself is true, not your confidence in the status label. Limited evidence can inform that number without establishing the claim. Cite exact source IDs for evidence that establishes the claim or its negation. Use an empty list if no decisive source ID is available. Do not invent identifiers. A handoff may summarize record material. A follow-up is a new source when present. In your note, briefly distinguish decisive evidence from provisional indications.

{"scenario":"Meadow Arts Centre","question":"Can the facilities team mark the room ready for an evening booking?","claims":{"A":"Room F had an evening booking at 19:00.","B":"The replacement microphone worked in Room F at the post-repair test.","C":"The Room F wall plate was intact at 15:00."},"handoff":"{\"claims\":{\"A\":{\"status\":\"supported\",\"citations\":[\"S1\"]},\"B\":{\"status\":\"unresolved\",\"citations\":[]},\"C\":{\"status\":\"contradicted\",\"citations\":[\"S2\"]}},\"note\":\"Claim A is supported by venue calendar records showing Room F booked at 19:00 (S1). Claim C is contradicted by a technician's photo showing a cracked wall plate at 15:00 (S2). Claim B remains unresolved as there is no direct evidence of a successful post-repair test of the replacement microphone in Room F; supplier receipt and coordinator's note suggest it likely works but do not confirm post-repair testing (S3).\"}","follow_up":{"S4":"the independent evening crew's signed Room F post-repair test records sound captured cleanly from the replacement microphone."}}
